name: RWA’s Saturday Night Fever: Championship Chaos

date.source: Not dated on the page itself. Year inferred, not printed on the page: the Saturday Night Fever tournament final's own text schedules a rematch "next week," which lands exactly on this document's own Friday Night Fury (12/19) card (the same Triple Threat, the same vacant title) — and the fed's own closure notice (home-page.html) dates its shutdown to February 1998, bounding the whole corpus to 1997-98. Friday Night Fury (1/31)'s own date is independently anchored the same way in this ledger's existing tier-1 pass.

matches.note: World Heavyweight Title tournament. Axon Blade won after Dani Exell crotched 2000 Man on the turnbuckle and Axon hit him with Exell's own loaded purse, unseen by the referee.
World Heavyweight Title tournament, by DQ — Deadpool ran in and pulled Malady off Longshot mid-cover.
World Heavyweight Title tournament. Nuke won via pinfall with the FallOut after a brief Kontra offensive spurt.
World Heavyweight Title tournament, by submission (Widow’s Peak) after Homeboy spent the early minutes rapping instead of wrestling.
D&D won via the Frankensteiner/Powerbomb combo on Shatterstar after Deathstrike was knocked to the floor.
World Heavyweight Title tournament. Danix tripped Malady, possibly breaking his nose; Axon hit three Axon-Saults but Malady no-sold the third and won with the Maladjuster.
World Heavyweight Title tournament, via the FallOut.
Stevens won by submission (Mangler hold), earning a World Heavyweight Title shot the following week.

For the vacant World Heavyweight Title. A 30-minute time-limit draw — Nuke kept the match clean rather than target Malady's taped, bloodied nose until late, and Malady reversed Nuke's running inverted piledriver into a head-spike victory roll for a 2¾ count. The title stayed vacant; the fed's own text schedules a Triple Threat rematch with Pete Stevens the following week.

appearances.note: Interfered as Danix for Axon Blade in both his own matches (the loaded-purse run-in against 2000 Man; tripping Malady in the Second Round).
Ran in on the Malady/Longshot First Round bout, pulling Malady off Longshot for the DQ.

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Kontra won via submission (2 Extreme). Bone-Crusher and Death & Destruction ran out after the bell but Kontra escaped through the crowd.

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Bishop walked out for the countout rather than engage, after a slow staredown with Jester.

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: BeefCarver won via pinfall (Sausage Grinding).

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: The Crow won via pinfall (the Humilator).
Deathstrike pinned Fission with a Tombstone piledriver; the win earned Shatterstar and Deathstrike a Texas Tornado match with Death and Destruction.
Longshot ran in, power-bombing Kiazyk on the outside so Deadpool could hit the Deadpool Drop for the pin.

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — Second Round Match
matches.note: Kontra kicked out of the Hand of Death twice before falling to a third.

matches.stipulation: U.S. Heavyweight Title Tournament — Second Round Match
matches.note: Twelve minutes into an even brawl, Death Jester's Covenant of Death (two hooded men and the Keeper) ran in and beat down both men; the fed's own President and security cleared them out and the tournament advanced neither man.

Danix again distracted the referee with a purse spot, but 2000 Man turned it around, knocking Axon out; when Axon appeared not to be getting up, he rolled him up for the pin instead. Unmasked at the fed's own President's demand: 2000 Man was billed as “Extremely Deadly Wrestling superstar Refugee,” and left the promotion.

For the vacant U.S. Heavyweight Title. BeefCarver hit Jester with a barbed-wire bat and the Crow followed with a chair shot while the Keeper distracted the referee; a winded Martel covered for the win.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title Triple Threat Match
matches.note: For the vacant title. Nuke hit both men with the running inverted piledriver and pinned Stevens with the FallOut after reversing the Mangler hold; Malady then countered Nuke's own piledriver with a head-spike victory roll and finished him with the Maladjuster for the title. Nuke offered a handshake; Malady left without taking it.

appearances.note: Ran in on the Kiazyk/Deadpool #1 contenders match to help Deadpool win.
Led the Covenant of Death's run-in on the BeefCarver/Crow no-contest.
Ambushed Death Jester with a barbed-wire bat during the U.S. Heavyweight Title final.
Chair-shot Death Jester during the U.S. Heavyweight Title final.
Accompanied Death Jester's Covenant of Death, including the run-in on BeefCarver and the Crow.
Interfered as Danix in the Axon Blade/2000 Man mask-vs-hair match.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Killer won via the Execution Tombstone; carried the vacant title belt to the ring beforehand, daring anyone to come take it.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Death Jester ran in on the outside brawl, slamming Cpl. Punishment with the Hand of Death before Chronos brought him back in for the pin.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Longshot dominated but argued with the referee at the wrong moment; Homeboy caught him with the Ghetto Blaster for the pin.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — First Round Match
matches.note: Bishop, scouting his own next-week opponent Eastwood from the aisle, stormed the ring and attacked him — the page's own text credits the interference with handing Eastwood the DQ win over Kontra. Kontra went on a post-match rampage at ringside, destroying tables.

Radiation Poisoning ran in for D&D; an unnamed 7'1" masked man then appeared and chokeslammed both Shatterstar and Deathstrike before D&D's own finisher ended it. Fission introduced Gangrene afterward as the newest member of the Nation of Devistation.
Longshot needled Deadpool from ringside until Kontra and Danix of Da Messiah ran him off; the distraction let Martel roll Deadpool up for the pin.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — Second Round Match
matches.note: Winner: Chronos via pinfall (Gorilla Press/Legdrop into the Magnum Bomb) — the page's own match heading reads "Killer def. Chronos," contradicting its own declared result; the explicit Winner line is followed here.

matches.stipulation: World Television Title Tournament — Second Round Match
matches.note: Homeboy won with the Ghetto Blaster after Eastwood got cocky with the advantage.

The match never officially started. An unnamed hooded man jumped BeefCarver with a steel chain; Sammie Curr and RIP of Body Count then came down on the Covenant of Death's own side, helping beat down BeefCarver and the Crow, while Death Jester worked the Crow's knee into the ring post. The fed's own President and security broke it up.
For the vacant World Television Title. Homeboy kicked out of one Magnum Bomb but fell to a second.

Billed "replacing Nuke": Axon Blade, Kontra and Danix jumped Nuke backstage before the match, leaving him unable to compete. Malady defended against Axon, the #1 contender, and won by DQ once Kontra and Danix jumped into the ring late in the match. Da Messiah then beat on Malady with his own title belt until Nuke, still staggered, ran out to help fend them off; Malady left without acknowledging him.

appearances.note: Ran in for Death and Destruction during the Texas Tornado match against Shatterstar and Deathstrike.
Ran in on the Chronos/Cpl. Punishment first-round bout, slamming Punishment with the Hand of Death.
Needled Deadpool from ringside during the U.S. Heavyweight Title match until run off by Kontra and Danix.
Ran off Longshot with Danix during the U.S. Heavyweight Title match, and interfered in the World Heavyweight Title match, jumping Nuke backstage and costing Axon Blade the title match by DQ.
Stormed the ring and attacked Joe Eastwood during Eastwood's own match against Kontra, which the page's own text credits with the DQ win for Eastwood.
Introduced Gangrene as the newest member of the Nation of Devistation after the Texas Tornado match.
Introduced as the newest member of the Nation of Devistation.
Interfered as Danix alongside Kontra, running off Longshot and jumping Nuke backstage.
Ran in on the Covenant of Death's own side during the 3-Way Dance of Death, helping beat down BeefCarver and the Crow.
Ran in on the Covenant of Death's own side during the 3-Way Dance of Death, pulling the Crow's arms during the beatdown.
Jumped backstage by Da Messiah before the World Heavyweight Title match, unable to compete; returned late, still staggered, to help Malady fend off Da Messiah.

name: RWA’s Friday Night Fury (1/31)

date.source: The fed’s own served broadcast title: "Friday Night Fury 1/31 - Part One."

matches.note: HellRaiser attacked before the bell and controlled the match; Spawn came back with a flying clothesline, a second-rope bulldog, and the Demon’s Death Drop for the pin.

Fucsko feigned interest in joining the Sinister Posse, shook hands with Homeboy, then lariat'd him and cleared Montreal Kid and Dan Tucker from the ring single-handed. He hit the Steel City Bomb, but the Posse ran back in and triple-teamed him — Fucsko was awarded the match by DQ.

Body Count (challengers) attacked before the bell. Sammie Curr blocked a Pleasure Wheel attempt with a Super Bomb; Cpl. Punishment ran in with a low blow on Paine so RIP could hit Rest In Pieces for the pin and the title.

appearances.note: Refereed the HellRaiser/Spawn opener.
Made ring introductions across the broadcast.
Conducted backstage interviews, including Longshot's own Triple Threat eulogy segment.
Appeared backstage with Canadian Homeboy and ran in on the Fucsko match.
Appeared backstage with Canadian Homeboy and ran in on the Fucsko match.
Accompanied Pleasure & Paine to the ring.
Accompanied Body Count to the ring.
Worked security, pulling the Keeper down off the ring apron.
Ran in on the World Tag Team Title match, hitting Jerry Paine with a low blow.
Cut a backstage promo declaring the Triple Threat dissolved and introducing three new, unnamed allies.

notes: Served as "Part One" only — the document's own text points to a "Friday Night Fury - Part 2" that is not held. Not present in this excerpt: the 25-man Battle Royal for the vacant World Television Title and the Nuke/Kontra Scaffold Match for the World Heavyweight Title, both previewed by the broadcast's own opening hype. Gap, not inferred: the Rankings page's own later snapshot shows Kontra as champion, but no held document records the Scaffold Match's own outcome.
